text: Meanwhile twenty one minutes before the train was due. <break time="0.8s" /> Six men were gathered. <break time="0.8s" /> At the bar of the Weary Gentleman saloon. <break time="0.8s" /> In Yellow Sky. <break time="0.8s" /> One was a drummer. <break time="0.8s" /> Who talked a great deal and rapidly. <break time="0.8s" /> Three were Texans. <break time="0.8s" /> Who did not care to talk. <break time="0.8s" /> And two were quiet Mexican sheep herders. <break time="0.8s" /> Suddenly a young man appeared. <break time="0.8s" /> At the open door. <break time="0.8s" /> And cried. <break time="0.8s" /> That Scratchy Wilson was drunk. <break time="0.8s" /> And had turned loose with both hands. <break time="0.8s" /> The two Mexicans at once. <break time="0.8s" /> Set down their glasses. <break time="0.8s" /> And faded out by the rear entrance. <break time="0.8s" /> While the bartender quickly closed. <break time="0.8s" /> And barred the heavy doors. <break time="0.8s" /> The puzzled drummer asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether there would be a fight. <break time="0.8s" /> And one man answered grimly. <break time="0.8s" /> That he did not know about a fight. <break time="0.8s" /> But there would be some shooting. <break time="0.8s" /> The men explained. <break time="0.8s" /> That Scratchy was the last of the old gang. <break time="0.8s" /> That used to hang out along the river. <break time="0.8s" /> And that he was a terror when drunk. <break time="0.8s" /> When he was sober. <break time="0.8s" /> He was the nicest fellow in town. <break time="0.8s" /> And would not hurt a fly. <break time="0.8s" /> But drink turned him. <break time="0.8s" /> Into a wild and dangerous man. <break time="0.8s" /> Only Jack Potter. <break time="0.8s" /> The town marshal. <break time="0.8s" /> Had ever been able to handle him. <break time="0.8s" /> And Potter. <break time="0.8s" /> As everyone knew. <break time="0.8s" /> Was away in San Antonio.
